questions_and_answers.question: What was the greatest political impact of the civil rights movement?
questions_and_answers.answer: I think the greatest impact of the civil rights movement is that it began to give African Americans some hope of full citizenship, and showed them that some whites were with them in the struggle. Dr. Martin Luther King knew that any kind of rights can’t really be just handed to people; people have to reach out and take them. After the Civil War and the Emancipation Proclamation, African Americans had some hope—dashed very quickly by every means certain white people could find, so that de facto segregation remained in place—and, as we’ve seen in recent months, still remains in place. Certainly the election of President Barack Obama (twice) was a great step forward—oh how I wish he were still president—he is so intelligent, so sane, so caring and reasonable. And certainly Congress’s passing of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was another step forward, as were the policies of President John F. Kennedy, and his brother, Attorney General Robert Kennedy. All of this is progress, but not enough,…

questions_and_answers.answer: I believe there was a sequence of events in the early 1960s leading to a "bending moment" of white resistance to the CRM that was profound and enduring. The Little Rock Nine and the Voting Rights Act of 1957 were just some of the critical events that led to that bending moment and one can hardly imaging the eventual progress of the 60s without them. questions_and_answers.question: What were the achievements of the Civil Rights Movement by 1968?
questions_and_answers.answer: By 1968, the civil rights movement had achieved significant legislative advances including the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which outlawed segregation and employment discrimination, the Voting Rights Act of 1965, protecting African Americans' right to vote, and the Civil Rights Act of 1968, which prohibited housing discrimination.

questions_and_answers.question: Create a short outline for an essay about the causes and effects of the civil rights movement. Your claim doesn't have to be argumentative, but it should say something that isn't obvious - something that needs to be backed up with reasons and evidence. In later lessons, you'll use your outline and research to draft your essay. Then you'll present that essay to the class. Your outline should include a claim that answers a research question, at least three main points that support your claim, and a list of sources that will provide evidence to back up your claim and main points. Make sure that your sources are reasonably up-to-date, published by trustworthy companies or organizations, transparent about where their information comes from, and written by an author who has some authority. Your outline should include the following elements: ﻿﻿A claim that answers your research question and says something interesting enough to justify a whole essay ﻿﻿At least three main points that support your claim ﻿﻿Citation information for at least three credible sources whose evidence backs up your claim or main points
questions_and_answers.answer: Essay Outline: The Civil Rights Movement Claim The Civil Rights Movement was not only a struggle for racial equality but also a catalyst for socio-economic changes in the United States, which had profound effects on the nation's political landscape. Main Points The Civil Rights Movement as a struggle for racial equality The movement was primarily aimed at ending racial segregation and discrimination against African Americans. Key events such as the Montgomery Bus Boycott, the March on Washington, and the Selma to Montgomery marches highlighted the struggle for racial equality. The Civil Rights Movement as a catalyst for socio-economic changes The movement led to significant changes in laws and policies, such as the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965. These changes had a profound impact on the socio-economic status of African Americans, leading to increased opportunities and improved living conditions. text_blocks.snippet: The Civil Rights Movement significantly impacted American society by dismantling legal segregation, securing voting rights, and expanding opportunities for African Americans. While it achieved landmark legislative victories and increased political representation, challenges like persistent racial inequality in areas like housing, education, and the justice system remain.
snippet_highlighted_words: dismantling legal segregation, securing voting rights, and expanding opportunities for African Americans

list.title: End of Legal Segregation:
list.snippet: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlawed segregation in public accommodations and employment, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 eliminated discriminatory voting practices.

list.title: Increased Political Representation:
list.snippet: The movement led to a rise in the number of Black Americans elected to public office.

list.title: Expanded Educational Opportunities:
list.snippet: The movement paved the way for integration in schools and increased access to higher education for African Americans.

list.title: Economic Gains:
list.snippet: Black Americans saw improvements in wages and income levels, and the movement helped break down barriers to employment.

list.title: Inspiration for Other Movements:
list.snippet: The Civil Rights Movement served as a model for other social justice movements, including those for Native Americans, Latinos, and women.

list.title: Persistent Inequality:
list.snippet: Despite legal advancements, racial disparities in wealth, income, housing, education, and the criminal justice system persist.

list.title: Resistance to Integration:
list.snippet: Some communities and institutions resisted integration, leading to continued de facto segregation in schools and neighborhoods.

list.title: Continued Voter Suppression:
list.snippet: While the Voting Rights Act addressed overt discrimination, efforts to suppress voting continue in various forms.

list.title: Racial Discrimination in Employment:
list.snippet: Despite legal prohibitions, discriminatory practices in the workplace persisted, particularly in certain industries.

list.title: Impact of Affirmative Action:
list.snippet: While affirmative action programs were introduced to address historical inequalities, they have also faced criticism and legal challenges.
